question: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 1,600 in two years and to Rs. 2,000 in three years at compound interest when compounded annually. Find the rate of interest.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In compound interest, the amount of the previous year acts as the principal for the next year.

For the 3rd year, Principal = ₹1600 and Amount = ₹2000.

Interest for 1 year = 2000 − 1600 = ₹400.

Rate = (Interest ÷ Principal) × 100

Rate = (400 ÷ 1600) × 100 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount in 2 years (A₂) = ₹1600

Amount in 3 years (A₃) = ₹2000

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)T

 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
 
 
 Start (P)
 End of Year 2
 End of Year 3
 Principal
 ₹1600
 ₹2000
 

 Interest = ₹400 (For 1 Year)
 Rate = (₹400 ÷ ₹1600) × 100 = 25%

**Calculations:**

⇒ A₂ = P(1 + R/100)² = 1600 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ A₃ = P(1 + R/100)³ = 2000 --- (Eq. 2)

Dividing Eq. 2 by Eq. 1:

⇒ [P(1 + R/100)³] ÷ [P(1 + R/100)²] = 2000 ÷ 1600

⇒ (1 + R/100) = 5/4

⇒ R/100 = 5/4 − 1

⇒ R/100 = 1/4

⇒ R = 100 ÷ 4 = 25%

**∴ The correct answer is 25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Successive Principal Concept

In compound interest, the total amount accumulated at the end of any period acts as the principal for the immediate next period.

Direct Rate Formula for Successive Years

When amounts for two consecutive years Aₜ and Aₜ₊₁ are given: Rate % = [(Aₜ₊₁ − Aₜ) ÷ Aₜ] × 100.

Compound Interest Formula

Total Amount A = P(1 + R/100)T, where P is the initial principal, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period in years.
